The mind: an answer with a shape

You will learn

Why a program asks an agent for an answer with a fixed shape, and how it refuses a reply whose shape is wrong.

When you chat with an agent you read free text. When a program reads the answer, free text is a problem: it cannot tell a sentence from a request to run something. So the agent is asked for a reply with a shape: a kind, and the arguments that kind needs. This spec has 3 kinds: 0 say, 1 ask and 2 call a tool. A sentence needs no argument; a question and a tool call need at least 1. The program checks the shape first and acts only if it fits. A tool call that names no file is refused before anything runs. The negative control plants the bug in one place: set NEEDS_CALL to 0 and the test the_bad_reply_is_refused turns red, because a reply with no arguments is no longer too short.

Try it

Open the widget and find which kind needs no argument; then run the spec, set NEEDS_CALL to 0, and read which test fails and why. Put the line back and run it again.

Three kinds of agent reply, how many arguments each needs, and the check a program runs before it acts on one. Lesson 19 of the Vibecoding from zero course.

specs/vibecoding/agent_mind.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/vibecoding/agent_mind.t27 -- vibecoding lesson 19: the mind of an agent, an answer with a shape.
; When a program has to read an agent's answer, free text is not enough: the agent hands back a
; reply with a fixed shape, a kind plus the arguments that kind needs. A program refuses a reply
; whose shape is wrong before it acts on it. Kinds: 0 say, 1 ask, 2 call a tool.
; A sentence needs no argument; a question needs one; a tool call needs at least one.
; Run the tests, then plant the bug named at the bottom and watch one test turn red.

module vibecoding_agent_mind;

pub const KIND_SAY : u8 = 0;
pub const KIND_ASK : u8 = 1;
pub const KIND_CALL : u8 = 2;
pub const KIND_COUNT : u8 = 3;

; Arguments each kind needs at least.
pub const NEEDS_SAY : u8 = 0;
pub const NEEDS_ASK : u8 = 1;
pub const NEEDS_CALL : u8 = 1;

; A good reply: a tool call that carries one argument (the file to read).
pub const GOOD_KIND : u8 = 2;
pub const GOOD_ARGS : u8 = 1;
; A bad reply: a tool call that names no file.
pub const BAD_KIND : u8 = 2;
pub const BAD_ARGS : u8 = 0;
; A reply of a kind that does not exist.
pub const ODD_KIND : u8 = 3;

test the_three_kinds_are_numbered_in_a_row {
    assert KIND_SAY == 0;
    assert KIND_ASK == 1;
    assert KIND_CALL == 2;
    assert KIND_COUNT == KIND_CALL + 1;
}

test a_sentence_needs_no_argument {
    assert NEEDS_SAY == 0;
}

test the_good_reply_has_enough_arguments {
    assert GOOD_KIND == KIND_CALL;
    assert GOOD_ARGS >= NEEDS_CALL;
}

; The negative control. The bad reply carries no argument and must be refused: it has fewer
; arguments than a call needs. Plant the bug by setting NEEDS_CALL to 0: this test turns red.
test the_bad_reply_is_refused {
    assert BAD_KIND == KIND_CALL;
    assert BAD_ARGS < NEEDS_CALL;
}

test an_unknown_kind_is_refused {
    assert ODD_KIND >= KIND_COUNT;
}
